parts.name: LiPo battery 4S 5200 mAh
parts.blurb: A rechargeable lithium-polymer battery pack: 4 cells in series, 14.8 V, lots of capacity.
parts.used_for: Main power source for medium ground robots.
parts.notes: Never discharge below about 3.0 V per cell; charge with a balance charger, never unattended. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo battery 4S 1500 mAh (5-inch quad)
parts.blurb: A smaller 4-cell LiPo pack sized for a 5-inch quadcopter.
parts.used_for: Flight battery for small quads where weight matters.
parts.notes: Flight packs work hard: retire a pack that comes down puffy or hot. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo battery 3S 2200 mAh
parts.blurb: A 3-cell LiPo pack, 11.1 V — the classic small-robot battery.
parts.used_for: Main power for small rovers, RC cars and servo robots.
parts.notes: Never discharge below about 3.0 V per cell; balance-charge only. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Buck converter 5 V / 5 A
parts.blurb: Steps a higher battery voltage down to a clean 5 V.
parts.used_for: Powers the computer and logic from the main battery.
parts.notes: Budget its current for the hungriest load — an SBC under load plus servos can brown out a weak converter. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo balance charger
parts.blurb: Charger that keeps every cell in a LiPo pack at the same voltage.
parts.used_for: Safely recharging LiPo packs between runs.
parts.notes: A balance charger is not optional for LiPo packs — it is how you avoid damaging cells. (General guidance.)

parts.name: XT60 pigtail lead
parts.blurb: A short lead with the yellow XT60 battery connector already soldered on.
parts.used_for: Connects the battery to the robot's power wiring.
parts.notes: XT60 is polarised, but check polarity before first plug-in — reversed power destroys electronics instantly. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Silicone wire 14 AWG (per metre)
parts.blurb: Flexible silicone-insulated wire thick enough for battery current.
parts.used_for: Main power runs between battery, fuse and drivers.
parts.notes: Match wire gauge to current: thin wire on a battery lead is a fuse you did not choose. (General guidance.)

parts.name: TB6612FNG dual motor driver
parts.blurb: A small dual motor driver: runs two DC motors forward, reverse and brake from logic signals.
parts.used_for: Driving the two (or four, with two boards) gearmotors of a small rover.
parts.notes: Rated about 1.2 A per channel continuous — right for small gearmotors, too small for big motors at stall. (General guidance.)

current_a_per_channel.quote: Output current maximum: 3 A per channel

parts.name: L298N dual motor driver module
parts.blurb: The classic red dual H-bridge module for two DC motors or one stepper.
parts.used_for: Cheap motor driving for school and hobby robots (it is the driver in the official Andino build).
parts.notes: It drops roughly 2 V across the bridge and runs hot, so motors see noticeably less than the battery voltage. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 4-in-1 ESC 45 A (BLHeli_S class)
parts.blurb: Four brushless speed controllers on one board for a quadcopter.
parts.used_for: Driving a quad's four brushless motors from the flight controller.
parts.notes: Match ESC current rating and cell count to motors and battery. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Brushed ESC 60 A (QuicRun 1060 class)
parts.blurb: A single brushed speed controller for an RC car's main motor.
parts.used_for: Lets a receiver/computer throttle one brushed motor.
parts.notes: Set its battery-type jumper correctly (LiPo cutoff) before first run. (General guidance.)

parts.name: ESP32 development board
parts.blurb: A Wi-Fi/Bluetooth microcontroller board — the robot's reflexes.
parts.used_for: Real-time jobs: motor PWM, encoder counting, sensor polling.
parts.notes: GPIO is 3.3 V logic and not 5 V tolerant — level-shift 5 V sensor outputs. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Teensy 4.1
parts.blurb: A very fast microcontroller board popular for precise motion control.
parts.used_for: Arms and robots that need many fast, timed control loops.
parts.notes: 3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040)
parts.blurb: Raspberry Pi's cheap dual-core microcontroller board.
parts.used_for: Small control jobs, custom sensor hubs, PIO-based timing tricks.
parts.notes: 3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Raspberry Pi 5
parts.blurb: A full Linux computer the size of a credit card.
parts.used_for: The robot's brain: ROS 2, cameras, mapping, decision-making.
parts.notes: Needs a stiff 5 V / 5 A USB-C supply; undervoltage shows up as throttling and random reboots. (General guidance.)

parts.name: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
parts.source: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet (DS-11105-001)

specs.ai_performance: up to 67 TOPS (8 GB, Super mode)

parts.blurb: A GPU computer module for robots that see: camera AI on a board the size of a laptop memory stick.
parts.used_for: The robot's AI brain: vision models, perception and decision-making, with a GPU a Pi does not have.
parts.notes: Module only — it needs a carrier board, and its 5 V input must be sized for the 25 W top power mode; a sagging supply shows up as shutdowns under load. (Per the NVIDIA data sheet.)

parts.name: microSD card 128 GB (A2/V30)
parts.blurb: The removable flash card a Raspberry Pi boots from.
parts.used_for: Operating system, code and logged data storage.
parts.notes: The card is the robot's hard drive — a spare imaged card is cheap insurance. (General guidance.)

parts.name: SiK telemetry radio pair (915 MHz)
parts.source: Holybro SiK Telemetry Radio V3 class
parts.blurb: A pair of long-range radio modems that make a wireless serial link.
parts.used_for: Telemetry and parameter tuning for drones/field robots at range.
parts.notes: The 915 MHz variant suits the Americas; other regions use 433/868 MHz variants. (General guidance.)

parts.name: ExpressLRS receiver
parts.blurb: A tiny ExpressLRS radio-control receiver.
parts.used_for: Manual RC control link for cars, quads and boats.
parts.notes: Receiver and transmitter must run compatible ELRS versions and the same binding phrase. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Intel RealSense D435 depth camera
parts.blurb: A stereo depth camera: sees colour plus distance per pixel.
parts.used_for: Obstacle avoidance, 3D mapping, grasping.
parts.notes: Needs USB 3 for full depth rates; depth is unreliable in bright sunlight and on glass. (General guidance.)

photo.note: SLAMTEC publishes renders, not photographs, of the A1 — labelled a render wherever it appears.

parts.name: RPLIDAR A1 2D lidar
parts.blurb: A spinning 2D laser scanner — it sweeps a room and reports distances all around.
parts.used_for: Mapping and localisation for indoor rovers (SLAM). It is the lidar on Andino and the TurtleBot3 class.
parts.notes: Keep its scan plane unobstructed for the full 360 degrees or the map gets blind spots. (General guidance.)

parts.name: BNO055 9-DOF IMU breakout
parts.blurb: A 9-axis motion sensor with on-chip orientation fusion (compass + gyro + accelerometer).
parts.used_for: Heading and tilt sensing for rovers, humanoids and arms. Also the IMU in the official Andino BOM.
parts.notes: Keep it away from motors and power wires — magnetic interference corrupts its heading. (General guidance.)

parts.name: HC-SR04 ultrasonic ranger
parts.blurb: The two-eyed sonar module: pings and times the echo to measure distance.
parts.used_for: Cheap short-range obstacle detection on a budget.
parts.notes: Its echo pin outputs 5 V — divide it down before a 3.3 V input. Soft or angled surfaces absorb/deflect the ping. (General guidance.)

parts.name: PLA filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: The standard easy-print 3D printing plastic, on a 1 kg spool.
parts.used_for: Chassis plates, brackets and mounts (like this catalogue's CAD-kit parts).
parts.notes: PLA is stiff and easy but softens in a hot car; PETG is the tougher choice for parts near motors. (General guidance.)

parts.name: PETG filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: A tougher, slightly flexible printing filament.
parts.used_for: Functional brackets and parts that take knocks.
parts.notes: Prints hotter than PLA and strings more; a dried spool prints noticeably better. (General guidance.)

bed_temp_c_max.quote: Bed temperature should be set between 60-70 °C.

bed_temp_c_min.quote: Bed temperature should be set between 60-70 °C.

parts.name: Inline blade fuse holder + fuse
parts.blurb: A fuse holder wired into the battery's main lead.
parts.used_for: The last line of defence against a short circuit cooking the wiring.
parts.notes: Size the fuse above normal draw and below the wire's rating. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Emergency stop button (latching)
parts.blurb: A big latching red button that cuts power when slapped.
parts.used_for: Emergency stop for arms, humanoids and anything that can pinch.
parts.notes: Wire it in the main power path, not in software — it must work when the code doesn't. (General guidance.)

parts.name: BMS protection board 4S 40 A
parts.blurb: A battery-management board that protects a 4-cell pack from over/under-voltage.
parts.used_for: Protection for DIY 4S packs built from bare cells.
parts.notes: A BMS protects the pack; it is not a charger — still use a proper balance charger. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Custom PCB (KiCad import)
parts.source: imported from the builder's own KiCad project
parts.blurb: Your own circuit board, designed in KiCad and fabricated to order.
parts.used_for: Tidying a proven breadboard design into one reliable board.
parts.notes: Prove the circuit on a breadboard first — a PCB faithfully reproduces design mistakes. (General guidance.)

photo.note: Class exemplar: a Pololu 37D x54L mm 12 V gearmotor — the catalogue records the generic 37 mm class.

parts.name: DC gearmotor 12 V (37 mm class)
parts.blurb: A DC motor with a built-in gearbox: slow, strong turning for wheels.
parts.used_for: Driving rover wheels — torque matters more than speed here.
parts.notes: Stall current is several times the running current — size the driver for stall or limit current. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Brushed motor 540 size
parts.blurb: The standard 540-size brushed motor from RC cars.
parts.used_for: Main drive motor in 1/10 RC cars.
parts.notes: Brushed motors spark and wear brushes; gearing decides whether it is fast or strong. (General guidance.)

parts.name: MG996R servo
parts.blurb: A metal-gear hobby servo that turns to a commanded angle.
parts.used_for: Steering, grippers, camera tilts, small arm joints.
parts.notes: Power servos from their own regulated rail, not a microcontroller pin — brownouts reset controllers. (General guidance.)

photo.note: Waveshare's ST3215 listing — the Feetech STS3215 serial bus servo.

parts.name: STS3215 serial bus servo (Feetech)
parts.blurb: A serial-bus servo: many chain on one wire and report their position back.
parts.used_for: Humanoid, quadruped and arm joints that need feedback.
parts.notes: Each bus servo needs a unique ID set before chaining; the bus is half-duplex UART. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Stepper motor NEMA 17
parts.blurb: A stepper motor that moves in precise 1.8-degree steps.
parts.used_for: 3D printers, CNC axes, precise positioners.
parts.notes: Needs a stepper driver (A4988/DRV8825 class) — never wire coils straight to a microcontroller. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Brushless motor 2207 1960 KV
parts.blurb: An FPV quad motor: small, light, spins very fast.
parts.used_for: One of four motors on a 5-inch quadcopter.
parts.notes: KV times battery volts is roughly unloaded RPM — match prop size to KV and cell count. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Wheel 100 mm diameter
parts.source: generic 100 mm robot wheel (pathfinder demo spec)
parts.blurb: A 100 mm robot wheel — the size on the Pathfinder spec.
parts.used_for: Main drive wheels for medium rovers.
parts.notes: Wheel diameter sets both ground clearance and the distance each motor turn travels — the motion gate measures exactly this. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Mecanum wheel 100 mm

specs.note: mecanum odometry is unreliable by design; gate heading checks differ

parts.blurb: A wheel with angled rollers that lets a robot slide sideways.
parts.used_for: Holonomic (any-direction) drive on flat floors.
parts.notes: Mecanum rollers make wheel odometry unreliable by design — expect heading drift and fuse with an IMU. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Ball caster
parts.blurb: A free-rolling ball that supports the end of a two-wheel robot without steering it.
parts.used_for: The third contact point on differential-drive robots like Andino and TurtleBot3.
parts.notes: Casters carry weight but no drive — the robot's balance point should sit close to the driven axle. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Propeller 5x4.0x3 tri-blade
parts.blurb: A 5-inch tri-blade propeller for FPV quads.
parts.used_for: Thrust for 5-inch quadcopters.
parts.notes: Props are the dangerous part of a quad — remove them for every bench test. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Flight controller stack F405
parts.blurb: Flight-controller board stack that stabilises a quadcopter.
parts.used_for: Reads the gyro, runs the control loop, drives the ESCs.
parts.notes: Mount it soft (vibration isolation) — a rigidly mounted gyro reads the frame's buzz as motion. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 2-finger parallel gripper kit
parts.blurb: A two-finger parallel gripper kit (servo not included).
parts.used_for: The hand on a robot arm.
parts.notes: Check servo torque against gripper + payload weight at full reach, not just at the base. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Quadcopter frame 5 inch (carbon)
parts.blurb: A carbon-fibre frame sized for 5-inch propellers.
parts.used_for: The skeleton of a freestyle quadcopter.
parts.notes: Carbon fibre is conductive — insulate every board and wire that touches the frame. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Aluminium extrusion 2020 (per metre)
parts.blurb: Slotted aluminium profile, 20 by 20 mm, sold by the metre.
parts.used_for: Frames for arms, gantries and test rigs.
parts.notes: Uses M3/M4 T-slot nuts — order fasteners when you order lengths. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Chassis plate (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: The flat deck everything bolts onto — in RobotForge it is generated for your robot, ready to print.
parts.used_for: The base layer of a ground robot: motors, battery and boards all mount to it.
parts.notes: Keep mounting holes a few millimetres from plate edges in printed plastic, and print flat-side down. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Motor mount bracket (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A small bracket that holds a gearmotor at exactly axle height.
parts.used_for: Bolting drive motors to the chassis plate.
parts.notes: Printed mounts flex under hard stall torque — gussets or a second bolt point help. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Lidar mount post (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A post that raises the 2D lidar above the deck for a clear 360-degree view.
parts.used_for: Mounting a spinning lidar on rovers.
parts.notes: The lidar must see over the robot's own body in every direction, or the map has a permanent blind wedge. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Camera bracket (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A small flat bracket that holds a camera facing forward.
parts.used_for: Mounting RGB/depth cameras on the chassis.
parts.notes: A slightly downward tilt sees near-field obstacles; level sees the horizon. Pick per job. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Ultrasonic bracket (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A twin-can bracket sized for an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic ranger.
parts.used_for: Holding an ultrasonic sensor square to the direction of travel.
parts.notes: Angle it straight ahead: a tilted sonar measures the floor, not the wall. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module V2 (8 MP)
parts.source: Raspberry Pi Camera Module V2 (the camera in the official Andino BOM)
parts.blurb: The little ribbon-cable camera made for the Raspberry Pi.
parts.used_for: Vision on Pi-based robots — it is Andino's camera.
parts.notes: The CSI ribbon is fragile and keyed — seat it straight and never hot-swap it. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 18650 Li-ion pack 3S (3 cells)
parts.source: generic 18650 cells in a 3-cell holder (the battery in the official Andino BOM)
parts.blurb: Three cylindrical 18650 cells in series — 11.1 V of robot power.
parts.used_for: Main battery for small rovers — Andino runs on exactly this.
parts.notes: Use matched cells from one batch, and a holder with a fuse or BMS for a robot that drives unattended. (General guidance.)

parts.name: SG90 micro servo
parts.blurb: A tiny 9 g positional servo, the classic first servo for small mechanisms.
parts.used_for: Steering, small grippers, camera tilt and sensor pointing on light robots.
parts.notes: Plastic gears strip under shock loads; keep loads light. (General guidance.) Interface: pwm.

parts.name: MG90S micro servo (metal gear)
parts.blurb: The SG90's tougher sibling: same size, metal gears, a bit more torque.
parts.used_for: Small mechanisms that outgrew plastic-gear servos.
parts.notes: Metal gears survive knocks better but still dislike stalled loads. (General guidance.) Interface: pwm.

parts.name: DS3218 high-torque servo (20 kg class)
parts.blurb: A standard-size digital servo with metal gears and serious holding torque.
parts.used_for: Arm joints, steering on heavier rovers, gripper actuation.
parts.notes: Draws amps in the plural at stall: power it from a real BEC, not a microcontroller pin. (General guidance.) Interface: pwm.

parts.name: 28BYJ-48 stepper motor with ULN2003 driver board
parts.blurb: A small 5 V geared stepper sold with its ULN2003 driver board; slow, cheap, everywhere.
parts.used_for: Dials, valves, small turntables and teaching rigs.
parts.notes: The 2048 steps per output revolution are in full-step mode through its 64:1 gearbox. (General guidance.)

parts.name: NEMA 23 stepper motor
parts.blurb: The bigger standard stepper frame: 57 mm face, 200 full steps per revolution.
parts.used_for: CNC axes, heavy gantries and larger arm joints.
parts.notes: Holding torque varies a lot by winding; check the datasheet of the exact unit before trusting it. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 25GA-370 DC gearmotor 12 V
parts.blurb: A 25 mm metal-gearbox DC motor, the workhorse size between toy motors and industrial ones.
parts.used_for: Medium rovers, conveyor drives and powered casters.
parts.notes: Sold in many gear ratios; the ratio, not the shell, sets speed and torque. (General guidance.)

parts.name: TT DC gearmotor (1:48, dual shaft)
parts.blurb: The yellow plastic-gearbox motor from classroom robot kits, with a shaft on both sides.
parts.used_for: First rovers and classroom kits; the free side takes an encoder disc.
parts.notes: Happy at 3-6 V; encoder discs for it are sold as a matching accessory. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 2212 1000KV brushless outrunner
parts.blurb: A classic mid-size drone and RC-plane outrunner, 1000 KV.
parts.used_for: Slow-flyer props, small VTOL and lift fans.
parts.notes: KV is rpm per volt unloaded; pick the prop for the cell count, not the other way round. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 775-size DC motor (12-24 V)
parts.blurb: A fist-sized brushed motor with real shaft power for tools and drivetrains.
parts.used_for: Spindles, pumps, heavy skid-steer drives.
parts.notes: Stall current is large; size the driver and fuse for it, not for the running current. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Hitec HS-645MG servo
parts.blurb: A long-running standard-size servo with metal gears, popular in RC and robotics.
parts.used_for: Steering and arm joints on mid-size robots.
parts.notes: Torque figure is the 6.0 V stall value from the datasheet; expect less in motion. (General guidance.) Interface: pwm.

parts.name: Linear actuator 12 V, 100 mm stroke
parts.blurb: A motor-driven pushrod: apply 12 V, it extends; reverse polarity, it retracts.
parts.used_for: Lifts, latches, dump beds and adjustable mounts.
parts.notes: Most have built-in limit switches at both ends of travel; speed drops as load rises. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Push-pull solenoid 12 V
parts.blurb: A coil and a spring-loaded plunger: power it and the plunger pulls in with a clack.
parts.used_for: Latches, pinball-style kickers, lock release and part ejectors.
parts.notes: Rated for intermittent duty; left powered, small solenoids cook themselves. (General guidance.)

parts.name: A4988 stepper driver (Pololu-style carrier)
parts.blurb: The little red stepper driver carrier: step/dir in, one bipolar stepper out, up to 1/16 microstepping.
parts.used_for: One NEMA-class stepper per board on small CNC and robot joints.
parts.notes: About 1 A per coil without a heatsink; set the current limit with the trim pot before first motion. (General guidance.)

parts.name: DRV8825 stepper driver (Pololu-style carrier)
parts.blurb: A4988's bigger sibling: higher voltage, 1/32 microstepping, more current per coil.
parts.used_for: NEMA 17/23 steppers that need more than an A4988 can give.
parts.notes: About 1.5 A per coil without forced cooling; it drops in where an A4988 sat, with different current-set maths. (General guidance.)

parts.name: TMC2209 silent stepper driver
parts.blurb: A stepper driver famous for quiet motion: stealthChop, sensorless homing, UART setup.
parts.used_for: Printers and robots that move near people and microphones.
parts.notes: Current figure is RMS per coil from the datasheet; quiet modes trade torque at speed. (General guidance.)

parts.name: BTS7960 43 A H-bridge module
parts.blurb: A chunky single-motor H-bridge module built around the BTS7960 half-bridges.
parts.used_for: One big brushed motor: 775s, wiper motors, actuator drives.
parts.notes: The 43 A figure is the chip's limit, not a promise at stall with no airflow. (General guidance.)

parts.name: PCA9685 16-channel PWM driver board
parts.blurb: An I2C board that runs 16 servos or LEDs with its own clock, so the microcontroller does not have to.
parts.used_for: Many-servo robots: hexapod legs, animatronics, arm arrays.
parts.notes: Servo power comes from the board's own terminal, not from I2C; budget a real 5-6 V supply. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c.

parts.name: L9110S dual H-bridge module
parts.blurb: A tiny two-motor driver for small voltages and small motors.
parts.used_for: TT motors and other toy-class drives on a budget.
parts.notes: Continuous current is under an amp per channel; stalled TT motors can still trip it. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 35 A BLHeli_32 ESC
parts.blurb: A single brushless ESC running BLHeli_32: configurable, DShot-capable, no BEC on most.
parts.used_for: Individual brushless motors outside a 4-in-1 stack.
parts.notes: Check whether the unit has a BEC before planning to power a receiver from it. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Arduino Uno R3
parts.blurb: The reference Arduino board: 5 V logic, a forest of shields, decades of examples.
parts.used_for: Teaching, prototyping and simple robot control at 5 V.
parts.notes: 5 V logic: level-shift before wiring it to 3.3 V sensors. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart/pwm.

parts.name: Arduino Nano (classic)
parts.blurb: Uno guts on a breadboard-friendly stick.
parts.used_for: Permanent small builds that started life as an Uno prototype.
parts.notes: Same 5 V logic and 16 MHz clock as the Uno; clones vary in USB chip. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart/pwm.

parts.name: STM32 Blue Pill board (STM32F103C8T6)
parts.blurb: A 72 MHz ARM Cortex-M3 board for a few dollars, programmed over SWD or USB.
parts.used_for: Fast control loops and CAN-bus nodes on a budget.
parts.notes: Boards vary in provenance; the USB resistor fix on early boards is well documented. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart/usb/can.

parts.name: ESP32-S3 development board
parts.blurb: The ESP32's newer sibling: dual-core, native USB, vector instructions for small ML.
parts.used_for: WiFi/BLE robot brains with camera and voice ambitions.
parts.notes: Native USB means it can present as keyboard/serial/MIDI without a bridge chip. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart/pwm/wifi/ble.

parts.name: NodeMCU ESP8266 development board
parts.blurb: The board that put WiFi on everything: one core, 3.3 V, huge community.
parts.used_for: Simple connected sensors and remotes.
parts.notes: One ADC pin and modest RAM: fine for telemetry, not for cameras. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart/pwm/wifi.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Pico W
parts.blurb: The Pico with WiFi and Bluetooth: RP2040 dual-core plus a radio.
parts.used_for: Connected controllers and robot nodes that phone home.
parts.notes: Same PIO superpowers as the plain Pico; radio and CPU share the board's power budget. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart/pio/wifi/ble.

parts.name: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040
parts.blurb: An RP2040 the size of a postage stamp, USB-C, for embedding in finished things.
parts.used_for: Wearables, in-mechanism controllers, tiny robot nodes.
parts.notes: Few pins is the point: plan the pin map before the enclosure. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi/uart.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
parts.blurb: The previous-generation Pi: quad-core, dual camera/display options, runs the same software as the 5.
parts.used_for: Robot brains where Pi 5 performance is not needed or stock is what it is.
parts.notes: Wants a real 5 V/3 A supply; undervoltage shows up as a lightning bolt and throttling. (General guidance.) Interface: usb/ethernet/csi/gpio.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
parts.blurb: A quad-core Pi in the tiny Zero footprint, with WiFi.
parts.used_for: Cameras and controllers in places a full Pi cannot fit.
parts.notes: 512 MB RAM is the ceiling; keep the workload honest. (General guidance.) Interface: csi/gpio/wifi/ble.

parts.name: NVIDIA Jetson Nano developer kit
parts.blurb: The original little Jetson: a 128-core Maxwell GPU for CUDA and vision learning.
parts.used_for: Vision projects and CUDA coursework on older, well-trodden docs.
parts.notes: Superseded by the Orin Nano for new designs; its software stack is frozen but deeply documented. (General guidance.) Interface: usb/ethernet/csi/gpio.

parts.name: Intel RealSense Depth Camera D455
parts.blurb: The long-range RealSense: depth from about 0.6 m to 6 m, with an IMU inside.
parts.used_for: Room-scale mapping, obstacle avoidance and the Scan Studio's measured scans.
parts.notes: The D455 is the camera Abel's scan bridge runs; depth error grows with distance (about 2% of range). (General guidance.) Interface: usb3.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3
parts.blurb: The current Pi camera: 12 MP with powered autofocus, in standard and wide versions.
parts.used_for: Robot eyes on any modern Pi.
parts.notes: Autofocus is the headline change from the v2; the ribbon is still fragile, route it kindly. (General guidance.) Interface: csi ribbon.

parts.name: OV5647 5 MP camera module (Pi camera v1 class)
parts.source: generic OV5647 module for Raspberry Pi
parts.blurb: The original Pi camera sensor on a module: 5 MP, fixed focus, everywhere.
parts.used_for: Cheap robot vision and timelapse rigs.
parts.notes: Fixed focus set at the factory; screwing the lens changes it permanently. (General guidance.) Interface: csi ribbon.

parts.name: Benewake TF-Luna LiDAR
parts.blurb: A single-point LiDAR the size of a grape: 0.2 to 8 m over UART or I2C.
parts.used_for: Altimeters, door counters and single-beam obstacle sensing.
parts.notes: Sunlight and dark surfaces shorten the practical range below the headline 8 m. (General guidance.) Interface: uart/i2c.

parts.name: VL53L0X time-of-flight distance sensor
parts.blurb: A laser ranging chip on a breakout: distance in millimetres over I2C, up to about 2 m.
parts.used_for: Precise short-range distance: gripper approach, wall following, fill levels.
parts.notes: Range depends on target reflectivity and ambient light; the datasheet's 2 m is the friendly case. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c.

parts.name: MPU-6050 6-axis IMU module (GY-521)
parts.blurb: The everywhere IMU module: 3-axis gyro plus 3-axis accelerometer on I2C.
parts.used_for: Balance, tilt sensing and motion logging on a budget.
parts.notes: No magnetometer: heading drifts without an external reference. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c.

parts.name: BME280 environmental sensor
parts.blurb: Temperature, humidity and air pressure from one tiny I2C chip.
parts.used_for: Weather stations, greenhouse robots and altitude estimates.
parts.notes: Self-heating biases the temperature reading if you sample it flat out. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c/spi.

parts.name: DHT22 / AM2302 temperature-humidity sensor
parts.blurb: The white-grid humidity and temperature sensor with the slow, patient protocol.
parts.used_for: Room and enclosure climate monitoring.
parts.notes: One reading every two seconds is its pace; it is not a control-loop sensor. (General guidance.) Interface: single-wire digital.

parts.name: INA219 current and voltage sensor board
parts.blurb: An I2C power monitor: bus voltage, current and power, read digitally.
parts.used_for: Battery telemetry and per-branch power budgets.
parts.notes: Figures are the chip's maxima from its datasheet (26 V bus, about 3.2 A with the fitted shunt). (General guidance.) Interface: i2c.

parts.name: u-blox NEO-M9N GPS module
parts.blurb: A modern multi-constellation GPS receiver on a breakout, with a real fix indicator.
parts.used_for: Outdoor navigation and geotagging.
parts.notes: Needs sky: indoors it will shrug at you. Cold starts take tens of seconds. (General guidance.) Interface: uart/i2c.

parts.name: Hall-effect motor encoder (pair)
parts.source: generic hall encoder kit for gearmotors
parts.blurb: Two hall sensors and a magnetic disc that clip onto a gearmotor's rear shaft.
parts.used_for: Wheel odometry for TT and 25GA-class motors.
parts.notes: Counts the motor shaft, not the wheel: gearbox backlash stays invisible to it. (General guidance.) Interface: digital pulse.

parts.name: QMC5883L 3-axis magnetometer
parts.blurb: A digital compass chip on a module: heading from the Earth's field, over I2C.
parts.used_for: Heading hold and turn-to-angle behaviours.
parts.notes: Motors and steel bend its world; calibrate away from both and mount it apart from them. (General guidance.) Interface: i2c.

parts.name: HC-SR501 PIR motion sensor
parts.blurb: The white-domed motion detector from a thousand alarm projects.
parts.used_for: Wake-on-approach, room occupancy and scarecrow duty.
parts.notes: Detects changes in infrared, i.e. warm things moving; a still person fades from its view. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Sharp GP2Y0A21YK0F IR distance sensor
parts.blurb: The classic analogue IR ranger: voltage out falls as the obstacle nears, 10 to 80 cm.
parts.used_for: Obstacle detection older and newer robots keep coming back to.
parts.notes: Inside 10 cm the reading folds back and lies; keep a bumper for the last centimetres. (General guidance.) Interface: analog voltage.

parts.name: HX711 load cell kit (5 kg cell + amplifier)
parts.source: generic HX711 + beam load cell kit
parts.blurb: A beam load cell and its 24-bit amplifier chip: weigh things with a microcontroller.
parts.used_for: Gripper force, hopper levels and thrust stands.
parts.notes: Accurate after a two-point calibration with a known mass, and not before. (General guidance.) Interface: 2-wire serial.

parts.name: LiPo battery 2S 5000 mAh
parts.blurb: A 2-cell lithium-polymer pack, 7.4 V, the RC car standard.
parts.used_for: RC cars, small rovers and 7.4 V servo systems.
parts.notes: Same LiPo rules as its bigger siblings: balance charge, never discharge below about 3.0 V per cell. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo battery 6S 1300 mAh
parts.blurb: A 6-cell pack for 5-inch and larger quads that want punch over endurance.
parts.used_for: Freestyle and racing quadcopters.
parts.notes: 6S on a motor/prop picked for 4S is a fire with extra steps; check the whole chain. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 21700 Li-ion cell 3.7 V (5000 mAh class)
parts.blurb: The bigger cylindrical cell: 21 by 70 mm, about 5000 mAh in current production cells.
parts.used_for: Custom battery packs and high-capacity handhelds.
parts.notes: Spot-weld, do not solder, cells; and buy cells with datasheets, not adjectives. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LM2596 adjustable buck converter module
parts.blurb: The blue adjustable step-down module with the trim pot: set the voltage, feed a robot from a bigger pack.
parts.used_for: Deriving 5 V or 12 V rails from a main battery.
parts.notes: The 3 A figure is the switch's; sustained output near it needs airflow and honesty. (General guidance.)

parts.name: MT3608 boost converter module
parts.blurb: A tiny step-up module: turn one cell's sagging voltage into a steady higher rail.
parts.used_for: Running 5 V or 12 V bits from a single Li-ion cell.
parts.notes: Boosting multiplies input current: a 2 A output at 12 V drinks far more at 3.7 V in. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Power distribution board with XT60 input
parts.blurb: A quadcopter power hub: battery in on XT60, solder pads out to ESCs and regulators.
parts.used_for: Multirotor power wiring without a knot of splices.
parts.notes: Pads are not fuses: the board distributes faults as happily as power. (General guidance.)

parts.name: iMAX B6 balance charger
parts.blurb: The long-running blue balance charger for LiPo/Li-ion/NiMH packs, 80 W class.
parts.used_for: Charging the packs in this catalogue on a bench.
parts.notes: Originals and clones share a name; the genuine article's menus are the documented ones. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 7805 voltage regulator (TO-220)
parts.blurb: The three-legged classic: a steady 5 V out, heat as the price of simplicity.
parts.used_for: Small 5 V rails where efficiency does not matter and silence does.
parts.notes: It burns the dropped voltage as heat: at 12 V in and 1 A out, that is 7 W looking for a heatsink. (General guidance.)

parts.name: NiMH battery pack 7.2 V, 3000 mAh
parts.blurb: A forgiving 6-cell nickel-metal-hydride pack, the old RC standard.
parts.used_for: Trainers, toys and robots that charge unattended-adjacent.
parts.notes: Less energy-dense than LiPo and much harder to set on fire: the school-club trade. (General guidance.)

parts.name: XT90 pigtail (12 AWG)
parts.blurb: The big sibling of XT60 on a short silicone lead, for high-current packs.
parts.used_for: 6S and larger power connections.
parts.notes: Match the connector to the worst current, not the average. (General guidance.)

parts.name: XT30 pigtail (18 AWG)
parts.blurb: The little XT: a compact 2-pin power connector on a silicone lead.
parts.used_for: Small quads and tidy low-current power runs.
parts.notes: XT30 is rated well below XT60; small connector, small currents. (General guidance.)

parts.name: JST PH 2.0 mm connector set
parts.blurb: Crimp housings and pins for the 2.0 mm pitch connector on half the sensor boards ever made.
parts.used_for: Making custom sensor and battery leads.
parts.notes: A proper ratchet crimper turns these from misery into routine. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Dupont jumper wire kit
parts.blurb: Rainbow ribbons of male-male, male-female and female-female jumpers.
parts.used_for: Breadboarding everything in this catalogue.
parts.notes: The female ends loosen with age and cause the best ghost faults in the hobby. (General guidance.)

parts.name: WAGO 221 lever-nut connectors (assortment)
parts.blurb: Lever-operated splicing connectors: flip, insert, clamp. Reusable and honest.
parts.used_for: Bench power distribution and quick rework.
parts.notes: Genuine 221s carry ratings printed on the body; unbranded lookalikes are a lottery. (General guidance.)

parts.name: USB-C to USB-C cable (100 W PD)
parts.blurb: A USB-C cable rated for 100 W power delivery, for hungry single-board computers.
parts.used_for: Powering a Pi 5 or Jetson properly instead of almost properly.
parts.notes: 100 W cables carry an e-marker chip; a random thin cable may cap you at 60 W or 3 A. (General guidance.)

parts.name: QWIIC / STEMMA QT cable set
parts.source: generic JST SH 1.0 mm I2C cable set
parts.blurb: Little 4-pin I2C cables in several lengths: sensor to board with no soldering.
parts.used_for: Chaining I2C sensors from SparkFun and Adafruit ecosystems.
parts.notes: QWIIC and STEMMA QT are the same connector and pinout wearing two badges. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Heat-shrink tubing kit (assorted)
parts.blurb: A box of shrinking sleeves in every diameter a robot harness wants.
parts.used_for: Insulating splices and finishing cable ends.
parts.notes: Adhesive-lined (3:1) shrinks are the ones that survive vibration and weather. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Rubber wheel 65 mm (TT-motor fit)
parts.blurb: The wheel that ships with every TT-motor kit: 65 mm of grippy rubber.
parts.used_for: Classroom rovers and light differential drives.
parts.notes: Hub fits the TT motor's dual-flat shaft; a screw through the hub stops the wobble. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Mecanum wheel 48 mm
parts.blurb: A small mecanum wheel: rollers at 45 degrees let a chassis strafe.
parts.used_for: Holonomic tabletop robots.
parts.notes: Sold as left/right handed rollers; a set needs two of each, mounted as an X or O pattern. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Pneumatic wheel 130 mm
parts.blurb: An air-filled wheel that floats over gravel and grass instead of rattling across them.
parts.used_for: Outdoor rovers on real ground.
parts.notes: Check the hub bore and axle standard before ordering the second pair. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Rubber tank track set (pair)
parts.blurb: Linked rubber tracks with drive sprockets and idlers for a tracked chassis.
parts.used_for: Skid-steer rovers that climb kerbs and loose ground.
parts.notes: Tracks steer by scrubbing: budget motor current for the turn, not the straight line. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Omni wheel 60 mm
parts.blurb: A wheel with free rollers around its rim: drives forward, slides sideways.
parts.used_for: Three-wheel holonomic (kiwi) drives.
parts.notes: Rollers find every cable tie and floor seam; keep its world tidy. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Aluminium extrusion 3030 (per metre)
parts.blurb: Slotted aluminium profile, 30 by 30 mm, sold by the metre.
parts.used_for: Stiffer frames, printer gantries and test rigs.
parts.notes: Uses M4/M5 T-slot nuts depending on slot series; confirm before the fastener order. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Aluminium extrusion 2040 (per metre)
parts.blurb: The flat 20-by-40 profile: a beam and a rail in one.
parts.used_for: Linear axes, camera sliders and long frame members.
parts.notes: Strong axis is the 40 mm direction; orient it against the load. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 608-2RS ball bearing
parts.blurb: The skateboard bearing: 8 mm bore, 22 mm outside, 7 mm wide, sealed both sides.
parts.used_for: Idlers, rollers, spool holders and cheap shafts everywhere.
parts.notes: The most standardised part in the catalogue: dimensions are the standard, brands are a detail. (General guidance.)

parts.name: GT2 timing belt 6 mm (open, per metre)
parts.blurb: Open-ended 2 mm-pitch toothed belt, 6 mm wide, sold by the metre.
parts.used_for: Linear axes and wheel-free drive runs.
parts.notes: Fibreglass-cored belt barely stretches; steel-core is stiffer and hates small pulleys. (General guidance.)

parts.name: GT2 pulley 20T, 5 mm bore
parts.blurb: A 20-tooth GT2 pulley with a 5 mm bore for NEMA 17 shafts.
parts.used_for: The motor end of a belt axis.
parts.notes: Two grub screws at 90 degrees is the good pattern; one screw walks loose. (General guidance.)

parts.name: T8 lead screw with brass nut (8 mm)
parts.blurb: An 8 mm trapezoidal screw and its anti-backlash brass nut, in axis lengths.
parts.used_for: Z axes, lifts and slow precise linear motion.
parts.notes: The common 4-start version advances 8 mm per turn; single-start (2 mm) exists and looks identical in photos. (General guidance.)

parts.name: MGN12 linear rail with carriage
parts.blurb: A 12 mm miniature linear guideway and its ball carriage block.
parts.used_for: Printer axes, camera sliders and anywhere a shaft-and-bushing wobbles too much.
parts.notes: The carriage balls are loose if it comes off the rail; the plastic keeper is not packaging. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Flexible shaft coupler 5 x 8 mm
parts.blurb: A spring-cut aluminium coupler joining a 5 mm motor shaft to an 8 mm screw or shaft.
parts.used_for: Stepper-to-leadscrew joints that forgive a little misalignment.
parts.notes: Forgiving of angle, honest about backlash: precision axes want it aligned anyway. (General guidance.)

parts.name: M3 brass standoff kit (assorted)
parts.blurb: Hex brass spacers in a ladder of lengths: how boards hover over plates.
parts.used_for: Stacking PCBs, flight controllers and sensor boards.
parts.notes: Nylon versions isolate electrically and strip if you look at them firmly. (General guidance.)

parts.name: M3 socket-head screw kit (assorted lengths)
parts.blurb: The box every robot builder ends up owning: M3 bolts from 6 to 30 mm, nuts and washers.
parts.used_for: Fastening printed parts, extrusion and boards.
parts.notes: Button-head for looks, socket-head for torque, and a spare box for the floor's share. (General guidance.)

parts.name: M3 heat-set thread inserts
parts.source: generic knurled brass inserts (CNC Kitchen pattern)
parts.blurb: Brass inserts that melt into printed holes and leave a real machine thread behind.
parts.used_for: Printed enclosures and parts that get disassembled more than once.
parts.notes: Hole diameter is insert-specific and smaller than intuition says; print a test coupon first. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 2020 corner bracket set
parts.blurb: Cast aluminium right-angle brackets that square up 2020 extrusion frames.
parts.used_for: Frame corners on rigs, enclosures and printer frames.
parts.notes: Cast brackets square a frame; printed ones mostly decorate it. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Carbon fibre tube 10 mm OD (per metre)
parts.blurb: A stiff, light 10 mm tube for booms, legs and handles.
parts.used_for: Drone arms, sensor masts and leg links.
parts.notes: Cut it wet or with extraction, and seal the dust: carbon splinters are forever. (General guidance.)

parts.name: ABS filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: The older workhorse plastic: tougher than PLA, warps without an enclosure.
parts.used_for: Parts that live near heat or outdoors-ish.
parts.notes: Vapour-smoothing is an acetone party trick, not a finishing plan. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Polycarbonate filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: The strong, heat-tough printing plastic: prints hot and warps if rushed.
parts.used_for: Gears, brackets and parts that live near motors or in hot cars.
parts.notes: Wants a hot bed, an enclosure and dry storage; wet PC prints like bubble wrap. (General guidance.)

parts.name: HIPS filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: ABS-like filament best known as a dissolvable support material.
parts.used_for: Support structures for ABS prints, and light housings.
parts.notes: Dissolves in d-limonene, which is the whole trick; as a print material it is ABS's quieter sibling. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Standard photopolymer resin, 1 kg (405 nm)
parts.blurb: Bottle of UV-curing resin for detail parts on an MSLA printer.
parts.used_for: Miniatures, fine gears and visual prototypes.
parts.notes: Uncured resin is a skin sensitiser: gloves, ventilation, and cure the waste. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Baltic birch plywood sheet 3 mm
parts.blurb: Void-free plywood that laser-cuts into beautiful chassis plates.
parts.used_for: Laser-cut rover decks and enclosures.
parts.notes: Real Baltic birch has the BB/BB stamp and no football patches on the good face. (General guidance.)

parts.name: nRF24L01+ 2.4 GHz radio module
parts.blurb: A tiny SPI radio that links Arduinos across a room for pocket money.
parts.used_for: Custom remotes and robot-to-robot chatter.
parts.notes: A capacitor across its power pins cures half the forum threads ever written about it. (General guidance.) Interface: spi.

parts.name: LoRa radio module 915 MHz (RFM95W)
parts.blurb: A long-range, low-rate radio: kilometres of telemetry at a whisper of power.
parts.used_for: Field robots and remote sensors far from WiFi.
parts.notes: 915 MHz is the Americas band plan; other regions differ and so do the rules. (General guidance.) Interface: spi.

parts.name: HM-10 BLE Bluetooth module
parts.blurb: A UART-to-Bluetooth-LE bridge: serial in, phone app out.
parts.used_for: Phone-controlled robots and wireless serial links.
parts.notes: Clones vary in firmware; the AT command set is the tell. (General guidance.) Interface: uart.

parts.name: SN65HVD230 CAN bus transceiver board
parts.blurb: A 3.3 V CAN transceiver on a board: how ESP32s and Teensys join a vehicle bus.
parts.used_for: Talking to smart servos, ESCs and vehicle networks.
parts.notes: A CAN bus wants its 120 ohm terminators at both ends, not at every node. (General guidance.) Interface: can.

parts.name: CP2102 USB-to-UART adapter
parts.blurb: The little USB stick that gives any UART a serial console.
parts.used_for: Debugging headless boards and flashing stubborn ones.
parts.notes: Check whether its logic jumper is at 3.3 V before it meets a 3.3 V board. (General guidance.) Interface: usb/uart.

parts.name: LiPo low-voltage alarm (1-8S)
parts.blurb: A beeper that rides the balance lead and screams before a cell sags too far.
parts.used_for: Any LiPo robot without telemetry.
parts.notes: Set it to 3.5-3.6 V per cell for warning with margin, not the 3.0 V of no return. (General guidance.)

parts.name: XT90-S anti-spark connector (pair)
parts.blurb: An XT90 with a resistor pre-charge path: no snap, no pitted contacts on big packs.
parts.used_for: 6S+ power connections with thirsty ESC capacitors.
parts.notes: Plug it in one motion; hovering at the resistor stage cooks the resistor. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Manual-reset circuit breaker 30 A
parts.blurb: A resettable breaker for the main battery line: pops on fault, presses back to life.
parts.used_for: Main power protection on mid-size rovers.
parts.notes: Size it above honest stall totals of everything downstream, below the wire's rating. (General guidance.)

parts.name: microSD card 256 GB (V30)
parts.blurb: A quarter-terabyte on a fingernail, fast enough for 4K logging.
parts.used_for: SBC storage, camera recording and dataset capture.
parts.notes: Endurance-rated cards survive logging duty; bargain cards become read-only art. (General guidance.)

parts.name: M.2 2280 NVMe SSD 1 TB
parts.blurb: A terabyte of fast storage for the SBCs that can boot from it.
parts.used_for: Jetson and Pi 5 data logging and dataset work.
parts.notes: Check the host's lane count before blaming the drive for its speed. (General guidance.) Interface: pcie nvme.

parts.name: Holybro Pixhawk 6C flight controller
parts.blurb: The current reference Pixhawk: triple-redundant IMUs, the full PX4/ArduPilot stack.
parts.used_for: Serious multirotors and VTOL research builds.
parts.notes: Abel's PX4 work is simulation-only; this is the hardware that stack targets. (Catalogue note.)

parts.name: Propeller 6x4 (pair)
parts.blurb: A 6-inch, 4-inch-pitch two-blade prop pair (CW + CCW).
parts.used_for: Park flyers and small pusher drones.
parts.notes: Props are consumables with a failure mode; inspect after every crash, retire after any strike. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Electromagnet 12 V (holding)
parts.blurb: A puck that becomes a magnet when powered: pick up steel parts, drop them on command.
parts.used_for: Pick-and-place of ferrous parts and magnetic latching.
parts.notes: Holding ratings assume thick, flat, clean steel; paint and gaps tax them hard. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Parallel gripper kit (servo-driven)
parts.blurb: Two fingers on parallel links that stay parallel: the honest way to hold a cube.
parts.used_for: Arm end-effectors and pick-and-place demos.
parts.notes: Link up a standard servo (MG996R class) and mind the finger pads' friction. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Perfboard / protoboard set
parts.blurb: Copper-dot boards in useful sizes: where a circuit goes when it graduates from the breadboard.
parts.used_for: Permanent one-off interfaces and sensor carriers.
parts.notes: One size up from the circuit you planned is the correct size. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 2306 1750KV brushless motor
parts.blurb: The 5-inch freestyle standard: 23 mm stator, 1750 KV for 6S manners.
parts.used_for: Freestyle quadcopters.
parts.notes: 1750 KV is the 6S tune; on 4S it will feel sleepy. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Robot Brain
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The V5 robot's computer: it runs your program and talks to every motor and sensor through its Smart Ports.
parts.used_for: The one controller on every VEX V5 robot.
parts.notes: Any Smart Port takes any Smart device (motor, sensor, radio); program it in VEXcode, PROS or vexide. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Smart Motor (11 W)
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: VEX's main motor: a motor, gearbox cartridge, encoder and controller in one box. Swap the cartridge to trade speed for torque.
parts.used_for: Drive trains, lifts, intakes and arms on V5 robots.
parts.notes: Red cartridge 100 rpm (most torque), green 200 rpm, blue 600 rpm (fastest). The motor limits its own current, so a stalled motor gets hot and slows down instead of burning out. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Smart Motor (5.5 W)
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: A smaller, half-power V5 motor with a fixed 200 rpm output.
parts.used_for: Light jobs like intakes and small mechanisms, so the 11 W motors can go to the drive.
parts.notes: Half the power of the 11 W motor. Competition rules cap the total motor power on a robot, so two 5.5 W motors count the same as one 11 W motor. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Robot Battery (Li-ion, 1100 mAh)
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The V5 battery pack. It plugs into the Brain, and the Brain powers every motor.
parts.used_for: Powers the whole V5 robot.
parts.notes: Charge it with the V5 charger only. Bring spare charged batteries to matches. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Controller
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The handheld controller the driver uses: two joysticks, buttons, and a small screen.
parts.used_for: Driving the robot during driver control.
parts.notes: Pairs with the Brain over the V5 Radio, or with a tether cable. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Robot Radio
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The radio that links the Brain to the controller.
parts.used_for: Wireless driving, and robot-to-robot messages with VEXlink.
parts.notes: Mount it where metal doesn't block it, away from the motors. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX 4 in omni-directional wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: A wheel with small rollers around its edge. It grips forward and back, and slides sideways.
parts.used_for: Tank drives that turn smoothly, and X-drives or H-drives that strafe.
parts.notes: The size is the nominal diameter; measure the real wheel before trusting speed numbers. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX 3.25 in omni-directional wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: A smaller omni wheel, a common choice for fast competition drive trains.
parts.used_for: 6-wheel V5 tank drives (often with traction wheels in the middle).
parts.notes: The size is the nominal diameter; measure the real wheel before trusting speed numbers. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX 2.75 in omni-directional wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The smallest VEX omni wheel, low and light.
parts.used_for: Compact drive trains and tracking wheels for odometry.
parts.notes: Often used unpowered with a Rotation Sensor as a tracking wheel. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX 3.25 in traction wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: A wheel with a grippy tread and no rollers, so it resists being pushed sideways.
parts.used_for: The middle wheels of a 6-wheel tank drive, to resist defence.
parts.notes: Use traction wheels in the middle and omni wheels at the corners so the robot can still turn. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX 4 in mecanum wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: A wheel with angled rollers. Four of them, each with its own motor, let the robot drive in any direction.
parts.used_for: Holonomic drive trains that strafe sideways.
parts.notes: Needs one motor per wheel, and the rollers must form an X when viewed from above. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX aluminum C-channel (1x2x1)
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The standard VEX frame rail: a U-shaped metal beam with square holes every half inch.
parts.used_for: Drive train rails, towers and arms.
parts.notes: Aluminum is lighter, steel is stronger. Cut to length and brace with screws and nuts. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX high-strength gears (12-84 teeth)
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Spur gears that change speed and torque between a motor and a wheel.
parts.used_for: Gearing a drive train up for speed or down for pushing power.
parts.notes: Speed ratio = driving teeth / driven teeth. 36 on the motor driving 60 on the wheel turns the wheel at 0.6x motor speed with 1.67x the torque. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Inertial Sensor
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Measures which way the robot is facing and how it is moving.
parts.used_for: Accurate turns and heading in autonomous routines.
parts.notes: Calibrate it while the robot sits still at the start of a match. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Rotation Sensor
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Measures how far a shaft has turned, even across power cycles.
parts.used_for: Tracking wheels for odometry, and arm or lift angles.
parts.notes: Pair it with an unpowered 2.75 in omni wheel for odometry. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Distance Sensor
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: A laser time-of-flight sensor that measures how far away an object is.
parts.used_for: Lining up with field walls and game objects.
parts.notes: Dark or shiny surfaces can read short; test on the real field elements. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX V5 Optical Sensor
parts.source: VEX Robotics V5 product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Sees colour, brightness and how close an object is.
parts.used_for: Sorting game objects by colour inside an intake.
parts.notes: Has its own LED; turn it on for steady readings. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ Robot Brain (2nd gen)
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The VEX IQ robot's computer: it runs your program and talks to motors and sensors through 12 Smart Ports. The 2nd generation Brain has an inertial sensor built in.
parts.used_for: The one controller on every VEX IQ robot.
parts.notes: Program it in VEXcode IQ (blocks, Python or C++). Any Smart Port takes any IQ Smart device. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ Smart Motor
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: VEX IQ's motor: a small motor, gearbox, encoder and controller in one plastic case. 120 rpm with no load.
parts.used_for: Drive wheels, arms, intakes and lifts on IQ robots.
parts.notes: VEX's ratings: 120 rpm free speed, 0.414 N·m stall torque, 1.4 W peak. VIQRC robots may use at most 6, plugged in or not. Gear it with IQ gears for more speed or torque.

parts.name: VEX IQ Robot Battery (Li-ion, 2000 mAh)
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The IQ robot's rechargeable battery: 7.2 V, 2000 mAh (the 2nd generation is Li-ion, the 1st was NiMH).
parts.used_for: Powers the IQ Brain and everything plugged into it.
parts.notes: 1st and 2nd generation batteries are both 7.2 V, 2000 mAh; VIQRC allows one IQ battery or six AA cells. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ Controller (2nd gen)
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: The handheld controller for driving an IQ robot. The 2nd generation pairs from the Brain's menu with no cable.
parts.used_for: Driver control in matches and testing.
parts.notes: VIQRC robots are driven with one IQ Controller. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ 200 mm travel wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: IQ's standard wheel: one turn rolls it 200 mm forward (about 64 mm across).
parts.used_for: Most IQ drive bases.
parts.notes: VEX sizes IQ wheels by travel per turn; the diameter is travel ÷ π. Measure the real wheel before trusting speed numbers.

parts.name: VEX IQ 200 mm travel omni wheel
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: An IQ wheel with rollers round its edge: it grips forward and back and slides sideways, so the robot turns smoothly.
parts.used_for: Turning-friendly IQ drives and strafing H-drives.
parts.notes: Often paired with plain wheels: omni on one axle, grippy on the other. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ beams and plates
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: IQ's plastic building pieces: beams and plates on a 0.5 in hole grid, joined with snap-in pins. No tools needed.
parts.used_for: Frames, arms and towers on IQ robots.
parts.notes: Every IQ part lines up on the same 0.5 in grid. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ gears (12, 36, 60 teeth)
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Plastic spur gears for IQ. Small driving big gives torque; big driving small gives speed.
parts.used_for: Drive gearing, arms and lifts.
parts.notes: Example: a 36-tooth gear on the motor driving a 60-tooth gear on the wheel gives 120 × 36 ÷ 60 = 72 rpm and 1.67× the torque. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ Pneumatics Kit
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Air-powered pistons for IQ: a pump fills the tank and a solenoid fires the cylinders. Fast, strong, two-position moves.
parts.used_for: Clamps, kickers and flip-outs that only need two positions.
parts.notes: VIQRC allows at most two air tanks and one air pump on a robot.

parts.name: VEX IQ Distance Sensor (2nd gen)
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Measures how far away an object is with a laser time-of-flight beam.
parts.used_for: Lining up with walls and game pieces.
parts.notes: Works best on flat targets facing the sensor. (General guidance.)

parts.name: VEX IQ Optical Sensor
parts.source: VEX Robotics VEX IQ (2nd generation) product documentation (vexrobotics.com, kb.vex.com)
parts.blurb: Reads colour, brightness and how close an object is, close up.
parts.used_for: Sorting game pieces by colour and spotting field lines.
parts.notes: Range is short: a few centimetres. (General guidance.)
